subject: Tenanting & Egress Assertion — Evidence and Threat Synopsis
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@praxishealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: security@praxishealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Praxis RFP — Appendix C (deployment isolation + egress)

Aditya,

Thanks for taking this on. Appendix C of our vendor assessment asks for the following deliverables to satisfy our architecture review: a clear network topology diagram annotated with tenant boundaries, an evidence packet enumerating controls that enforce per-tenant egress (including how we prevent cross-tenant data exfiltration), a short threat-model summary (top 3 realistic attack paths and mitigations), and any audit/log samples showing egress decisions.

Timing: can you provide a draft packet by EOD Tuesday (Praxis time)? We want to review internally and include in our vendor scorecard.

We care particularly about:
- How you separate model-serving compute from customer data paths.
- Mechanisms that prevent a compromised model worker from establishing outbound tunnels.
- How operator/admin interfaces are scoped and logged.

If you have a one-page executive summary up-front that maps controls to the risk statements, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

—Laura
Laura Chen
Security Architect, Praxis Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@praxishealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Praxis RFP — Appendix C (deployment isolation + egress)

Laura —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass evidence packet that includes: an annotated network map, a controls index mapped to your risk statements, an operational overview of our service-anchored egress proxies, and a short threat synopsis focused on lateral escalation and outbound channeling. Highlights up-front:

- Tenant enforcement: per-tenant policy evaluation occurs at two layers — (1) the request-router and tokenization layer (which strips and validates tenant context), and (2) the egress-proxy layer where per-tenant allowlists and rate limits are enforced. We use policy hashes stored in the control plane; changes are pushed atomically to dataplane nodes.
- Egress hardening: each GPU worker sits behind a transparent sidecar egress proxy. The proxy enforces eBPF filters at the node NIC and validates TLS certificate pins for allowed endpoints. Workers have no direct SNAT to the public internet.
- Compromise scenarios: to mitigate a worker-level compromise we rely on ephemeral identity (short-lived mTLS certs tied to workload ids), automatic KV cache eviction on redeploy, and outbound flow guardrails that only permit pre-approved CIDR ranges or named external hosts.

Attachments included (draft): tenanting-egress-evidence-v1.pdf, network-map-annotated.svg.

Kimberly and Monica — please see inline notes where I call out open items (e.g., sample audit tail redaction and a concise language for the exec summary). If you can review by EOD Monday I’ll incorporate and send to Praxis.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Praxis RFP — Appendix C (deployment isolation + egress)

Aditya — quick pass from architecture:

Thanks for the draft. A few suggested edits and asks before we hand this to Praxis:

1) Network diagram: add the control-plane isolation path (separate subnet + HSM-provisioned certs) and mark which subnets are customer-facing.
2) Threat summary: reframe "compromise" scenario to show "chain of mitigations" (isolation -> identity -> egress guard -> detection). Praxis likes explicit mitigations per-step.
3) Audit tails: provide a redacted example that shows a denied egress decision with timestamp, policy-id, workload-id. We should redact IPs but keep hostnames.
4) Ops play: include the operator RBAC table (roles + least privilege) as a one-paragraph appendix.

I made small text edits and added a one-paragraph "operational assurance" note about automatic rollback on control-plane mismatch (helps their compliance folks). Also recommend we call out that dedicated/private deployments can opt into VPC peering & private link if they need fully customer-controlled egress.

I'll attach my annotated copy in the drive link (internal). Monica — can you produce the redacted audit example and short RBAC table? I can incorporate tonight.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@praxishealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Jun 2028 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Praxis RFP — Appendix C (deployment isolation + egress)

Laura —

Appended: updated evidence packet (praxis_evidence_index.pdf) which supersedes the previous draft. Key deliverables included:

1) Executive mapping (1 page) — control vs. risk mapping requested in Appendix C.
2) Annotated topology (network-map-annotated.svg) — shows control-plane segmentation, operator jump-host boundaries, sidecar egress proxies, and optional VPC peering lane for dedicated customers.
3) Threat synopsis (2 pages) — three primary attack paths we considered: misrouted tenant headers, stolen workload identity, and covert outbound tunneling via allowed hosts. Each path lists detection and automatic rollback actions.
4) Redacted audit sample (pdf) — example denied egress entry: timestamp, policy-id: PX-EG-94, workload-id: wkld-7f2a (redacted), target-host: vault.example.com (allowed), denied-host: suspicious.example.net (redacted ip).
5) Ops assurances & RBAC snapshot — short table of operator roles and the two-person approval step for control-plane policy pushes.

Notes on technical controls (short):
- Sidecar egress model: sidecars enforce per-tenant allowlists and signature-based host validation. Sidecars publish decisions to an append-only audit tail that is sharded per-tenant; the control plane retains hashes for tamper evidence.
- Node hardening: we instrument eBPF at the NIC to enforce outbound socket-level policies so even if a local process attempts raw sockets the kernel denies flows against the policy store.
- Fallbacks: when a policy mismatch or suspicious flow is detected, requests are rate-limited and the workload is placed into a quarantine tier pending automated remediation; traffic for other tenants on the same node continues on validated paths.

Links: drive packet: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/px-4321/evidence-v1; HubSpot record: HS-Record-238721.

We hope this addresses Appendix C. If you'd like, we can run a short walkthrough of the packet (20-30 mins) with our security engineering team. Otherwise let us know any gaps and we'll follow up.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
